title: BC private managed forest land
description: The practice requirements for a block on private managed forest land outside a tree farm licence, woodlot licence and community forest agreement area, where the Private Managed Forest Land Act applies and FRPA’s forest practices do not: roads and trails held to the minimum, roads kept back from classed streams, crossings, sediment, drinking water and licensed intakes, tree and understory retention by stream class, reforestation by Coast and Interior density, and critical wildlife habitat. Stream classes are the Council Regulation’s Schedule, by channel width, for fish streams and streams above a licensed waterworks intake; the reviewer classes each stream. Every rule applies only when the land status review answers that the land is private managed forest land.

relatedPacks.relationship: Its managed-forest-land rule says when this pack’s rules are the block’s; the two questions are asked once and shared (sameAs).

choices: Federal land, including an Indian reserve
facts.label: What land is the block on? Crown land is land vested in the provincial government (the Land Act meaning, Forest Act §1); private land is land that is not Crown land. A reserve and treaty settlement land are asked apart: these packs do not assess them.

Is the block’s private land private managed forest land: land under a management commitment and classified as managed forest land under the Assessment Act (PMFLA §1), or land classified as managed forest land when the Act came into force and deemed so without a commitment (§45)?
Is the block in the area of an area-based licence (Forest Act §1), on its Crown land or on private land the licence includes?
Is the land on the Coast, the area of the former Coast Forest Region, or in the Interior, the rest of the province (Council Matters Regulation §1)?
Is the cutblock beside a class A stream: a fish stream, or a stream above a licensed waterworks intake, with a channel 10 m wide or wider (Council Regulation Schedule §1(1)(a))?
Is the cutblock beside a class B stream: a fish stream, or a stream above a licensed waterworks intake, with a channel 3 m wide or wider but narrower than 10 m (Schedule §1(1)(b))?
Is the cutblock beside a class C stream: a fish stream, or a stream above a licensed waterworks intake, with a channel 1.5 m wide or wider but narrower than 3 m (Schedule §1(1)(c))?
Is that class C stream’s gradient more than 8% (Council Regulation §29(3)–(4))?

Is the cutblock beside a class D stream (a fish stream, or one above a licensed waterworks intake, narrower than 1.5 m) or a class E stream (1.5 m wide or wider and flowing directly into a class A, B, C or D stream) (Schedule §1(1)(d), (2))?
Will a road be built within 30 m of a class A or B stream, or within 10 m of a class C, D or E stream, slope distance (Council Regulation §16)?
Will a road or logging trail cross a stream with a bridge, culvert or ford (Council Regulation §17)?
Is there a drinking water intake, licensed for a domestic or industrial purpose and drunk by people, whose water the block’s harvesting, roads or silviculture could reach (Council Regulation §14.1)?
Will a road be built within 100 m upslope, slope distance, of a licensed waterworks intake (Council Regulation §20(2))?

Has the wildlife minister given the owner notice establishing critical wildlife habitat on the land, a notice that names the area where road building and harvesting must be modified (PMFL Regulation §§5, 7)?
Does the owner know that the land may hold habitat for a species on the ministry’s published list of species at risk without enough habitat on Crown land in the ecoregion (PMFL Regulation §8)?

rules.title: Roads and logging trails held to the minimum
rules.finding: Productive forest land in the cutblock converted to roads, and to logging trails, must be held to the minimum necessary for safe and efficient harvesting, and logging trails rehabilitated as far as reforestation needs, unless a trail is expected to serve ground beyond the cutblock. The regulation states no figure: the road area the planner measures is evidence for the reviewer’s judgement, never a pass or fail.

actions.description: Compare the block’s road and trail area with what safe and efficient harvesting needs, and plan the trails’ rehabilitation.

exceptions.label: Only to the extent needed to prevent damage to the environment from occurring or continuing, or to protect the public’s safety (§3(3))
evidence: The damage or hazard, and why departing from the requirement was needed

rules.title: No road within 30 m of a class A or B stream, or 10 m of a class C, D or E stream
rules.finding: A road may not be built within 30 m (slope distance) of a class A or B stream, or within 10 m of a class C, D or E stream, unless keeping the distance would risk more sediment reaching the stream, there is no other practicable place for the road, or the road is part of a stream crossing.

actions.description: Move the road out of the distance, or record which of §16(f)–(h) applies and why.

exceptions.label: Keeping the distance would create a higher risk of sediment reaching the stream than not keeping it (§16(f))

rules.title: A crossing protects the channel and banks
rules.finding: A bridge, culvert or ford on a road or logging trail must be located, built and used so it protects the channel and banks immediately above and below it and mitigates disturbance at it, as far as needed to avoid a material adverse effect on fish habitat or on water a licensed waterworks intake diverts; a logging trail’s crossing is removed once the owner no longer needs it. The regulation authorizes no change in and about a stream: that needs the Water Sustainability Act (§2(1)).

actions.description: Design and build the crossing to protect the channel and banks, hold the Water Sustainability Act authority for it, and plan a trail crossing’s removal.

rules.title: At least 30 trees kept beside each 100 m of a class A stream
rules.finding: On each side of every 100 m of a class A stream beside the cutblock, at least 30 trees are kept, chosen in turn: trees 30 cm or more, then 20 cm or more, within 10 m of the channel edge, then within 20 m, then within 30 m, keeping the stand’s mix of conifers and broadleaves and, for the larger trees, its range of sizes; where fewer qualify, all that do. They are spread along the 100 m unless the other bank meets the count and the species do not suit partial cutting, and one may be removed only if it falls naturally outside the channel. Hybrid poplar and cottonwood plantations on the lower Fraser are excepted (§27(6)).

actions.description: Select and mark the trees to keep on each side of every 100 m of the class A stream before falling.

rules.title: At least 15 trees kept beside each 100 m of a class C stream
rules.finding: On each side of every 100 m of a class C stream beside the cutblock, at least 15 trees 20 cm or more in diameter within 10 m of the channel edge are kept, keeping the stand’s mix of conifers and broadleaves and its range of sizes; where fewer qualify, all that do. Where the stream is steeper than 8%, a kept tree may be cut only if another 20 cm tree is kept in its place; at 8% or less, one may be removed only if it falls naturally outside the channel.

rules.title: Restocked within 5 years and regenerated within 15 (Interior)
rules.finding: The harvested area, less its roads and logging trails, must be restocked within 5 years of harvesting’s completion with at least 600 crop trees a hectare reasonably well distributed, and hold a successfully regenerated stand within 15 years: at least 600 crop trees a hectare that are taller than the competing vegetation within 1 m by 25%. Crop trees are commercial species the management commitment names. Harvesting is complete on the date the owner’s annual declaration gives, or at most two operating seasons after it began.

actions.description: Plan restocking to 600 crop trees a hectare within 5 years and the stand’s care to 15 years.

exceptions.label: The area harvested or destroyed is a contiguous area under 1 ha (§31(2)(a))
evidence: The area’s measured size

exceptions.label: The trees left on the area already make a successfully regenerated stand (§31(2)(b))
evidence: A survey of the residual stand against the density and height tests

exceptions.label: The area harvested becomes occupied by buildings or other structures or installations (§31(6)(b))

rules.title: Harvest and roads in critical wildlife habitat follow the minister’s notice
rules.finding: Inside critical wildlife habitat the wildlife minister established, harvesting and road building must follow the notice’s requirements. Unless the owner agreed otherwise, the area to be modified is at most the lesser of 1% of the land in the management commitment and the area the species needs, and modified operations last at most a year; the requirements take effect 14 days after the owner receives the notice, or on the date the minister names.

actions.description: Read the notice and plan the harvest and roads to its requirements.

rules.title: Possible habitat of a listed species: notify, and hold off
rules.finding: An owner who knows the land may hold habitat for a species on the ministry’s list must promptly notify the wildlife minister and hold off road building and harvesting that could harm it until 14 days after the minister receives the notice, the minister says the work may go ahead, or a notice establishing critical wildlife habitat arrives, whichever is first.

actions.description: Notify the wildlife minister, and hold the work that could harm the habitat until one of §8(2)(b)’s three events.

exceptions.label: The wildlife minister relieved the owner of notifying for the species (§8(3))
evidence: The minister’s relief and the species it names
